headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: ChatGPT Desktop can read local/app content while Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate from a persistent cloud workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while Replit Agent can write and modify workspace files. If content from one is copied into the other, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the bridge is indirect rather than automatic.
conditions: IF content from Replit workspace files is pasted or uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop
IF ChatGPT Desktop output is copied into Replit files and later parsed as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary: paste only plain text, never executable snippets.
Add a human review step before Replit Agent acts on any ChatGPT-generated instructions.
Keep prompt-like content in separate files from code files.
Disable clipboard bridging during agent handoff where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags or file labeling between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and both touch sensitive classes: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code; Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. A shared workspace or manual transfer can expose sensitive data across vendors. The profiles do not show a direct shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the same secret, codebase, or deployment config is copied into both agents
IF ChatGPT Desktop is given screenshots or uploaded files containing secrets that are then transferred into Replit
mitigations: Do not place secrets in files shared between the agents.
Redact screenshots and uploads before sending them to ChatGPT Desktop.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive tasks.
Rotate any secret exposed to either agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret-scanning at transfer points.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has shell, package install, git modification, and filesystem write; ChatGPT Desktop can read files and interact with supported macOS apps, but the pair still overlaps on mutable code artifacts through file access and manual transfer. Because Replit persists workspace state and can modify git, concurrent edits can overwrite each other. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or workspace files
IF Replit Agent commits or rewrites files while ChatGPT Desktop is using copied file contents
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only for the shared repo.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same files.
Run a quick diff before accepting either agent's changes.
requires-engineering: add file locking or merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived summaries that Replit Agent may use to continue implementation. Replit Agent has authority to execute shell commands and modify git state, so unverified ChatGPT output can cascade into real changes. The profiles do not show a mandatory verification gate, but the pathway is not fully automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent is instructed to implement or commit based on ChatGPT Desktop output without review
IF ChatGPT Desktop summaries are treated as authoritative inputs to Replit actions
mitigations: Require a human to verify ChatGPT outputs before Replit acts.
Ask Replit Agent to restate assumptions before editing files.
Keep a checklist for claims that need source verification.
Review diffs before any commit or deployment.
requires-engineering: add automated citation or provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive data handling and retention, even though the profiles do not specify exact residency or certification gaps. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets, customer data, or deployment configs is processed by both agents
IF organizational policy requires a single residency or retention regime across tools
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to both agents.
Classify data before handing it to either agent.
Keep a written retention rule for each workspace.
Review vendor terms for the specific data class.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a single compliant environment.
